problem: The point $Q$ has cylindrical coordinates $(5,\pi ,7).$ Find the Cartesian coordinates of $Q.$
worked_solution:
If $(r,\theta ,z)$ are the cylindrical polar coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,z=z
$$

Calculating $x$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =5\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi ) \\  & =5\cdot (-1) \\  & =-5.\end{aligned}
$$

Calculating $y$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =5\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi ) \\  & =5\cdot 0 \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the Cartesian coordinates of $Q$ are $(-5,0,7).$
